newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico December open unemployment falls to 4.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico December open unemployment falls to 4.1 pct.

text.p: Mexico's open, or base, unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent during December compared with 4.8 percent in the month before, the National Statistics Institute said on Monday.
It said this was the lowest unemployment rate in the last 24 months.
In the latest Reuters survey, analysts expect the unemployment rate to drop to 4.54 percent on average.
The jobless rate compared with 5.5 percent unemployment during month of December 1995.
INEGI defines open unemployment as members of the workforce older than 12 who have searched for work but have not worked more than one hour a week during a month.

The Rate of General Pressure, which measures those in work looking for a new job as well as open unemployment, was 6.8 percent during December last year, compared with 9.2 percent in December 1995, INEGI said in a statement.

The Rate of Partial Joblessness and Unemployment, which includes open unemployment and those who have worked less than 35 hours a week due to market conditions, fell to 5.6 percent during December versus 7.8 percent in the same month a year earlier.

The Alternative Open Unemployment Rate, which includes open unemployment as well as those who have given up looking for work, was 4.8 percent in December compared with 6.9 percent in December a year earlier.
